summary: Three distribution lists for sending out Network documents such as RFCs, covering sites, the Network Information Center and station agents. These were postal addresses, not email lists. It replaced RFC 211 and was replaced by RFC 303.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 300 lists postal recipients for network documents and explains which of three lists a sender should use. It replaced RFC 211 and was later replaced by RFC 303.

questions: what are the three arpanet mailing lists
subtitle: Three postal mailing lists for distributing ARPANET documents

tldr.problem: The network needed recipient lists for sites, other participants and station agents who received formal documents.
tldr.mechanism: Sites use List A for their own documents; the NIC uses Lists B and C to distribute copies to non-site participants and station agents.
tldr.outcome: RFC 300 replaced RFC 211 and was later replaced by RFC 303.

facts.label: Station-agent mailing frequency
facts.value: Once a week or more often when quantity warrants

sections.title: Using the Mailing Lists
sections.content:
RFC 300 provides three lists for distributing network documents. Sites use List A when distributing their own documents, to get RFCs to liaisons quickly. All mail other than local mail should be sent by air mail.

The NIC uses Lists B and C to send copies to non-site network participants and station agents. The RFC replaces RFC 211.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites use List A to send their documents to liaisons. The NIC uses Lists B and C to reach other participants and station agents.

sections.title: Liaisons and Other Participants
sections.content:
List A includes all network liaisons and other initial recipients of RFCs, whether the documents come from a site or the NIC. These recipients also receive selected catalogs and formal documents from the NIC.

List B is for network participants who receive formal NIC documents. The RFC supplies names and postal addresses for contacts on both lists.
sections.plainLanguage: List A identifies the first recipients for RFCs. List B identifies other network participants who receive formal documents from the NIC.

sections.title: Station Agents and Successor
sections.content:
List C names NIC station agents. They receive copies of documents distributed to liaisons and items sent as part of a station collection. The NIC says it mails to station agents once a week, or more often when the quantity warrants.

The unit metadata records RFC 303 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 300.
sections.plainLanguage: List C identifies station agents who receive copies for their sites. RFC 303 later replaced this mailing list.

references.text: North, J. B., "ARPA Network Mailing Lists," RFC 211, August 1971.
